## Judgment

### Expected-drift set

`core-tpm2` is imported only by sweet16 and petunia (`grep -rn core-tpm2 hosts/`);
avina and hermes are Proxmox LXC with no TPM and do not import it. Adding
`ddukes` to `security.tpm2.tssGroup` therefore changes `/etc/group` and the
user-activation script on exactly those two hosts.

Expected: sweet16 DRIFT, petunia DRIFT, everything else zero.

This is the reason the option lives on `core-tpm2` rather than `core-users` —
declaring the group membership fleet-wide would have drifted avina and hermes
for a capability they cannot use.

### Actual vs expected

Matches exactly. `verify-drift.sh 2e92d01 HEAD`:

- sweet16 DRIFT, petunia DRIFT
- avina, hermes, groot@dualie, groot@forge: identical drv paths
- groot@rk3588 N/A (aarch64, not evaluable on this builder — pre-existing)

Effect confirmed by direct evaluation of `users.users.ddukes.extraGroups`:

- sweet16: `tss` present
- petunia: `tss` present (alongside its existing `openrgb`)
- avina: `tss` absent

No udev rule was added. `security.tpm2` already emits
`KERNEL=="tpmrm[0-9]*", MODE="0660", OWNER="root", GROUP="tss"`, so membership
is the entire mechanism; a second rule would only have raced the first on
udev's last-match-wins ordering.

sweet16's three `nix-nexus.*` assignments were collapsed into a single block to
satisfy statix W20 (triggered at three occurrences). Attrset merge, no
semantic change — consistent with the zero unexpected drift observed.

### Not yet exercised

Group membership requires a fresh login session to take effect, and this commit
has not been deployed to either host. The TPM capability probes
(`ssh-tpm-keygen --supported`, `tpm2_getcap properties-variable`) and the
LUKS keyslot check remain outstanding as Phase 0 gates.
